name: MCP23017 16-bit I/O expander
description: Microchip 16-bit I/O expander with an I2C interface: two 8-bit ports (GPA0-7, GPB0-7), each pin an input (optional 100 kOhm pull-up) or an output sinking/sourcing up to 25 mA, with two interrupt outputs. Runs on 1.8-5.5 V. Sold as: CJMCU-2317 MCP23017 module (three 10-pin headers: GND, VCC, SCL(/SCK), SDA(/SI), NC/CS, NC/SO, RESET, A0, A1, A2 | GND, ITA, GPA0-GPA7 | VCC, ITB, GPB0-GPB7; 10k pull-ups on SDA, SCL and RESET, A0-A2 pulled low), I2C address 0x20 (0x20-0x27 via A0-A2).
eli5: Gives your board 16 extra pins to switch LEDs or read buttons, using only the two I2C wires.

supplierQuery: CJMCU-2317 MCP23017 I2C 16-bit IO expander module
buildNotes: I2C address is 0x20 + (A2 A1 A0): the CJMCU-2317 pulls A0-A2 low through 10k, so it answers at 0x20 until you tie address pins to VCC.
All pins start as inputs (IODIR = 0xFF). Clear a bit in IODIRA (0x00) / IODIRB (0x01) to make that pin an output, then set it in OLATA (0x14) / OLATB (0x15).
Read pin levels from GPIOA (0x12) / GPIOB (0x13). Set GPPUA (0x0C) / GPPUB (0x0D) bits for the internal 100 kOhm pull-ups, e.g. for a button to GND.
GPA7 and GPB7 are output only on the MCP23017 (datasheet rev D): don't use them for buttons.
Each pin sources or sinks at most 25 mA and the whole chip 125 mA in / 150 mA out: always put a resistor in series with an LED.
The board's SDA/SCL pull-ups go to VCC: power it from 3.3 V when using an ESP32 or Pico so the bus never sees 5 V.
NC/CS and NC/SO are unused on the I2C chip; RESET is already pulled high, leave it unconnected.

driver.code:
# MCP23017 16-bit I2C I/O expander (Microchip DS20001952), MicroPython driver.
# Uses the power-on register map (IOCON.BANK = 0, sequential addressing):
#   IODIRA 0x00 / IODIRB 0x01  1 = input (reset value 0xFF), 0 = output
#   GPPUA  0x0C / GPPUB  0x0D  1 = 100 kOhm pull-up on an input
#   GPIOA  0x12 / GPIOB  0x13  read = the level on the pins
#   OLATA  0x14 / OLATB  0x15  output latches (what output pins drive)
# Pins are numbered 0-15: 0-7 = GPA0-GPA7, 8-15 = GPB0-GPB7.
# Note: on the MCP23017 (not the SPI MCP23S17) GPA7 and GPB7 are output only (datasheet rev D).

_IODIRA = 0x00
_IOCON = 0x0A
_GPPUA = 0x0C
_GPIOA = 0x12
_OLATA = 0x14

INPUT = 1
OUTPUT = 0


class MCP23017:
    def __init__(self, i2c, addr=0x20):
        """addr = 0x20 + A2A1A0 (0x20 with all address pins low, as on the CJMCU-2317)."""
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr
        # IOCON = 0: BANK = 0 (A/B registers paired), sequential addressing, INT pins active-low push-pull.
        self._w(_IOCON, 0x00)

    def _w(self, reg, val):
        self.i2c.writeto_mem(self.addr, reg, bytes([val & 0xFF]))

    def _r(self, reg):
        return self.i2c.readfrom_mem(self.addr, reg, 1)[0]

    def _bit(self, base, pin, on):
        if not 0 <= pin <= 15:
            raise ValueError('pin must be 0-15')
        reg = base + (pin >> 3)  # A register, or the B register right after it
        v = self._r(reg)
        v = v | (1 << (pin & 7)) if on else v & ~(1 << (pin & 7))
        self._w(reg, v)

    def pin_mode(self, pin, mode, pullup=False):
        """mode INPUT or OUTPUT; pullup enables the internal 100 kOhm pull-up (inputs only)."""
        if mode == INPUT and (pin & 7) == 7:
            raise ValueError('GPA7/GPB7 are output only on the MCP23017')
        self._bit(_IODIRA, pin, mode == INPUT)
        self._bit(_GPPUA, pin, pullup)

    def value(self, pin, val=None):
        """Read a pin's level (GPIO register), or set an output pin (OLAT register)."""
        if val is None:
            reg = _GPIOA + (pin >> 3)
            return (self._r(reg) >> (pin & 7)) & 1
        self._bit(_OLATA, pin, val)

    def read_port(self):
        """All 16 pin levels: bits 0-7 = GPA, bits 8-15 = GPB."""
        d = self.i2c.readfrom_mem(self.addr, _GPIOA, 2)  # GPIOA then GPIOB (auto-increment)
        return d[0] | (d[1] << 8)

    def write_port(self, val):
        """Set all 16 output latches: bits 0-7 = GPA, bits 8-15 = GPB."""
        self.i2c.writeto_mem(self.addr, _OLATA, bytes([val & 0xFF, (val >> 8) & 0xFF]))

    def config_port(self, iodir, pullups=0):
        """16-bit direction (1 = input) and pull-up masks in one go."""
        self.i2c.writeto_mem(self.addr, _IODIRA, bytes([iodir & 0xFF, (iodir >> 8) & 0xFF]))
        self.i2c.writeto_mem(self.addr, _GPPUA, bytes([pullups & 0xFF, (pullups >> 8) & 0xFF]))

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from mcp23017 import MCP23017, INPUT, OUTPUT

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
io = MCP23017(i2c)                   # address 0x20 (A0-A2 low)
io.pin_mode(0, OUTPUT)               # GPA0 drives an LED (through a resistor)
io.pin_mode(8, INPUT, pullup=True)   # GPB0 reads a button wired to GND
while True:
    pressed = 1 if io.value(8) == 0 else 0
    io.value(0, pressed)             # LED on while the button is held
    print('BTN=%d LED=%d' % (pressed, pressed))
    time.sleep_ms(200)
